concepts.name: Desktop workspace
concepts.initial_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished, complete, straight-on desktop application screenshot for a Mac/Windows Electron app called "GOG Achievements". Landscape, approximately 1440 by 900, the whole window fills the image. This is a design candidate, with fictional sample data, not a marketing page. The app restores achievements a user already earned. Clear real UI typography, generous but useful space, practical React/CSS components, code-native controls in the eventual app. Show "Cyberpunk 2077", signed-in label "GOG account 123456789", library search, Refresh, and the three sample queued achievements "The World", "Frequent Flyer", "The Wandering Fool". Their editable requested dates are "10 Oct 2026 18:30", "11 Oct 2026 20:10", "12 Oct 2026 19:15". Label the zone "Europe/London (UTC+01:00)". Existing unlocked achievements have a clear read-only state. Use plain language, readable dates, consistent subtle line icons, and high-contrast type. The only primary action at this editing stage is "Preview changes"; an "Apply changes" action, if shown, is disabled until preview. Show an actionable "Set date for selected" control and a remove control for queue entries. Library sample titles may include "The Witcher 3" and "Stardew Valley". Keep hidden achievements labeled "Hidden achievement" with a "Reveal" control. No made-up success metrics, percentages, backend details, logs, tokens, IDs used as decorative labels, reset/unlock-all buttons, extra unrelated navigation, marketing hero, invented slogans, floating decorative pills, excessive gradients, neon glows or fake dashboard charts. All text must be legible. No perspective, monitor hardware, hands, surrounding room, presentation board, or external caption.
Direction A: calm, precise desktop utility. Three visible vertical panes: a compact library at left, a roomy achievement list in the middle, a persistent editable queue at right. Cool white main canvas #FFFFFF, subtle cool-gray library #F2F4F8, ink text #1D2635, muted text #617087, thin dividers #E0E5ED, restrained plum accent #7150A2. IBM Plex Sans-style clear humanist UI lettering and small tabular date text. Header contains only product title and account menu; keep task controls inside the relevant pane. In the centre, selected game title, "Locked", "Unlocked", "Queued" filters, simple flat list rows with checkboxes and clear selected/queued states. Include the three queued names above plus "Legend of The Afterlife" locked, "Full Body Conversion" unlocked, and one concealed hidden achievement. The right pane is titled "Queue" and "3 achievements", with three clean name-and-date editor rows, bulk date control, and a plum "Preview changes" button fixed near the bottom. Every row has enough room; not nested cards. Distinctive signature: aligned checkboxes connect the selected achievement list to the editable queue without clutter. Native-feeling rounded controls of 6px and very restrained shadows. Keep it polished, confident, easy to scan and appropriate for a small reliable tool.
edit_prompts: Edit this desktop UI concept, preserving its light three-pane layout, colors, sizes, typography, game art, all three queue names and dates, timezone and bottom buttons. Make only these corrections: remove all achievement description sublines from the central list so it shows names and status only; remove the publisher subline beneath Cyberpunk 2077; remove numeric counts from the All/Unlocked/Locked/Queued filters; remove dotted drag handles beside the three queue entries (reordering is not a supported feature). Add a modest disabled "Add selected" button in the central achievement toolbar because the visible selected rows are already queued. Make the queued rows visibly checked but unavailable for duplicate addition, the "Legend of The Afterlife" row selectable and Locked, and "Full Body Conversion" visibly read-only with a disabled gray checkbox and text "Unlocked 04 Oct 2026". Keep "Hidden achievement" concealed with only its title and "Reveal" control; remove advice to keep playing. Do not invent extra controls, descriptions or metrics. Keep Preview changes enabled and Apply changes disabled. Keep every queue date readable.

Make one precise edit to this existing UI mockup. Preserve all layout, fonts, colors, icons, text, row sizes, names and dates. In the RIGHT queue pane, add a clearly visible checked purple selection checkbox in the spare left gutter of EACH of the three queue rows, to the left of its achievement thumbnail. These select queue rows for the existing Set date for selected action. Keep thumbnails, achievement names, date fields and remove icons aligned cleanly with enough space. Do not add checkboxes anywhere else or change any other part of the mockup. Keep Preview changes enabled and Apply changes disabled. This is a high-quality desktop app concept with crisp readable controls.

Direction B: an elegant dark game-library workspace. Deep aubergine graphite background #211F2A, raised surfaces #2D2938, muted lavender separators #494054, clear off-white type #F4F1F7, restrained pale lilac action #BBA4E6. Humanist title lettering with a slightly condensed game title and clean UI sans-serif. Left rail shows a compact game library with small tasteful cover thumbnails and selected Cyberpunk 2077. In the central work area put one modest panoramic atmospheric sci-fi city artwork strip for the selected game, no characters or spoilers, with readable "Cyberpunk 2077". Direction C: a focused restoration ledger, clearly different from a three-pane tool. Clean pale blue-gray canvas #F4F7FB, white working surface, dark navy ink #172C43, muted blue-gray #62758B, precise blue action #346A9D, thin separators #D6E1EB. Source Sans 3-style typography and Source Code Pro-style tabular timestamps used sparingly. Compact library sidebar at left. The rest of the window is one wide task area, with "Cyberpunk 2077" and a truthful ordered navigation "Select", "Dates", "Review"; "Dates" is the current stage. Main heading "Queue dates", with "3 achievements" and zone label. Show a generously spaced full-width table with columns "Achievement", "Unlock date", "Time", "Time zone" and row remove controls. All three sample queue rows are visible; selection checkboxes let the user choose rows, a "Set date for selected" control is above the table. Show dates as editable fields and offset "UTC+01:00" clearly, not as tiny metadata. A quiet read-only line indicates existing unlocked achievements keep their dates. Bottom action area: "Back to achievements", "Draft saved", and a clear blue "Preview changes". Signature: exact editable date columns and a staged task flow make review feel calm and deliberate. Rounded controls 4px, flat surfaces, minimal decorative iconography. Do not use faux spreadsheets with dozens of unreadable rows, a decorative paper texture, serif newspaper headlines or dashboard cards.

Remove the invented "42 already unlocked" count in the informational row, while preserving "Existing unlocked achievements keep their dates". Set the three queue-row selection checkboxes and the header checkbox to checked, so Set date for selected is clearly usable for this example.
